commit.message:
arch: arm64: save Xen-provided guest FDT

Preserve the FDT pointer handed to the boot CPU in x0 and copy the blob
after early data initialization. Keep the path optional behind
CONFIG_SAVE_XEN_FDT so non-Xen boot flows are unchanged.

The saved copy gives Xen guest code access to the exact device tree that
the hypervisor generated for this domain. Zephyr normally consumes the
compiled-in devicetree produced at build time, so the boot-time Xen FDT
is otherwise lost before later driver or test code can inspect it.

That matters for Xen validation tests. A Zephyr guest can parse this
saved blob to check which memory ranges, interrupt mappings, grant-table
regions, event-channel information, and Xen-specific nodes were actually
supplied by the hypervisor. This lets tests validate Xen's guest
description contract from inside the running guest, instead of relying
only on host-side launch configuration.

Signed-off-by: svlad-90 <svlad1990@gmail.com>

summary: This report is the final PR #139 review-fix interdiff: it compares the original upstream PR snapshot with the pushed FDT-only branch and shows the exact changes that are intended for the Xen FDT PR.

summary_blocks.body: Final scope: this report compares PR #139 as fetched from xen-troops/pr-139 with the pushed FDT-only branch svlad-90:store-xen-fdt. The report intentionally contains only the Xen FDT fixes. The SMP/per-vCPU event-channel work was removed from this branch and kept for the separate SMP PR.

What changed: the early assembly handoff now writes to internal z_arm64_* symbols, the C implementation keeps raw boot data separate from the validated saved FDT copy, runtime users get a documented public accessor, and debug-only boot printing was removed. The copied FDT is validated before it becomes visible to consumers.

diagram_notes.text: At reset time the code only preserves Xen handoff data. It does not expose that raw pointer as the public runtime contract.
The C boot path runs after data and BSS initialization, validates the raw handoff, and creates the Zephyr-owned copy.
Runtime consumers receive the stable copy and its validated byte count instead of touching early boot state directly.

summary_blocks.body: Runtime evidence: the final QEMU/Xen probe booted Zephyr under Xen 4.19.5, read the saved FDT through the public API, checked the FDT magic, totalsize, selected nodes, and FDT_END marker, then printed FDT PROBE PASS. QEMU was stopped by the safety timeout only after the pass marker was emitted.

fdt-api-runtime.title: QEMU/Xen 4.19 FDT API final runtime probe

arch/arm64/core/prep_c.c.body: This file now depends on the public Xen FDT header instead of a local extern. The boot hook remains in the same early C position: after BSS and data initialization, before the rest of arm64 startup continues.

arch/arm64/core/reset.S.body: This file now only preserves the Xen boot handoff in internal z_arm64_* symbols. The secondary-CPU guard that belongs to the later SMP/vCPU work is intentionally absent from this FDT-only PR.

arch/arm64/core/xen/fdt.c.body: This implementation separates raw reset-time state from the validated runtime copy. Invalid magic or oversize blobs panic before copying; valid data is copied once and returned through a narrow accessor.

include/zephyr/xen/fdt.h.body: This new public header is the review-facing API boundary. It documents both the runtime accessor and the early boot hook, including the meaning of a reported size of 0.

inline.title: Use the public FDT API header
inline.body: The startup code now includes the Xen FDT header instead of declaring xen_copy_fdt() locally. That makes the boot hook visible through the same contract that runtime users include, so declaration drift is avoided.

inline.title: Copy after early memory initialization
inline.body: xen_copy_fdt() still runs after arch_bss_zero() and arch_data_copy(). This matters because the assembly handoff is stored in .noinit, while the final saved FDT copy is ordinary Zephyr-owned storage. The runtime probe validates this ordering by reading a complete FDT through the public API after boot.

inline.title: SMP-only guard removed from this PR
inline.body: The previous cbz x0 secondary-CPU guard is not part of this FDT-only PR anymore. It belongs with the separate SMP/vCPU event-channel series, where secondary CPU entry is introduced and validated.

inline.title: Keep reset-time handoff internal
inline.body: The assembly path stores Xen's x0 handoff pointer in z_arm64_xen_fdt_addr. The z_ prefix marks this as Zephyr-internal startup state, not a public runtime symbol. Runtime code should use get_xen_fdt_ptr() after xen_copy_fdt() has validated and copied the blob.

inline.title: Raw handoff state is separate from runtime state
inline.body: The .noinit variables hold exactly what reset.S captured before normal C memory initialization. They are intentionally not the API consumed later by Xen code. The final runtime state is the validated xen_fdt copy and xen_fdt_size below.

target.content: /* Raw early-boot handoff from reset.S. Survives data/BSS initialization. */
target.diff_line: +/* Raw early-boot handoff from reset.S. Survives data/BSS initialization. */

inline.title: Expose a narrow runtime accessor
inline.body: get_xen_fdt_ptr() returns the Zephyr-owned copy and optionally reports the validated byte count. This avoids exporting the raw early-boot address and gives later code a stable contract.

inline.title: Validate before copying
inline.body: The code checks the FDT magic and maximum configured size before copying data. That prevents a bogus Xen handoff pointer or corrupt size field from becoming a trusted runtime FDT.

inline.title: No redundant full-buffer zeroing
inline.body: The extra arch_early_memset() was removed. The code records the number of valid bytes copied, so consumers should use xen_fdt_size rather than assuming the whole CONFIG_XEN_FDT_MAX_SIZE buffer is meaningful.

inline.title: Document the public FDT contract
inline.body: The public header now explains what the accessor returns, when the size output is valid, and what a size of 0 means. This is the part future Xen code should include instead of depending on internal startup symbols.

inline.title: Document the early boot hook
inline.body: xen_copy_fdt() is documented as an arm64 startup hook, not a general runtime API. That keeps the split clear: startup code copies and validates, runtime code calls get_xen_fdt_ptr().

story.title: Confirm the PR scope
story.body: Start with the assembly diff: it shows that the FDT PR now preserves only the Xen boot handoff. SMP secondary-CPU handling is no longer part of this branch.

story.title: Preserve Xen handoff data
story.body: The boot CPU receives the guest FDT pointer in x0. reset.S saves that raw pointer and the raw totalsize field into internal .noinit storage before normal C initialization can overwrite regular memory.

story.title: Copy after memory init
story.body: z_prep_c() calls xen_copy_fdt() after BSS zeroing and data copying. This ordering is the reason the final saved FDT copy is not erased by startup initialization.

story.title: Separate raw and runtime state
story.body: The implementation keeps raw .noinit handoff values separate from the validated Zephyr-owned runtime FDT copy. This addresses the review concern about confusing similarly named variables.

story.title: Reject invalid handoff data
story.body: Before copying, xen_copy_fdt() checks the FDT magic and makes sure the reported size fits CONFIG_XEN_FDT_MAX_SIZE. Bad input panics early instead of becoming runtime state.

story.title: Expose a documented API
story.body: The new public header documents get_xen_fdt_ptr() for consumers and keeps xen_copy_fdt() described as an early boot hook.

story.title: Inspect the end-to-end flow
story.body: Open the sequence diagram from the summary or comments to see how Xen's x0 handoff becomes a stable Zephyr-owned FDT pointer returned to runtime code.

story.title: Finish with runtime proof
story.body: The embedded QEMU/Xen log proves that the pushed branch boots, reads the saved FDT through the public API, validates key nodes, and reaches FDT PROBE PASS.
